sources.version_or_commit: Version 3, approved 2021-04-26
sources.locator: Printed pp. 6–9, 12, 22–26; Parts I and III
sources.governing_meaning: The BWF guidance distinguishes recommendation levels. BEXT Description and OriginatorReference have 256/32 ASCII-character limits; identifiers may point outward, with a pathname-security caution. FADGI interprets origination date/time locally, without unambiguous UTC. The ltxt recommendation permits tran and recommends ASCII free text linked to cue ranges, with termination/padding conditions. Its optional Code Page entry has an ISO 8859/1 fallback when CSET is absent or zero. Thus the ASCII recommendation is not proof of an ASCII-only implementation for every ltxt tool. These are embedding conditions, not a recorder-wide compatibility result.
sources.applicability: Supports the bounded BWF profile and timed-transcript lead. The final’s short-segment choice is a pilot recommendation, not a normative length cap.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 7–10; §1.1, §2.1, §2.3; Appendix A1 p. 15
sources.governing_meaning: BWF extends RIFF/WAVE using bext. Older readers ignore later UMID/loudness fields; early devices may not recognize later chunks. None of this proves arbitrary editor write behavior.

sources.version_or_commit: RFC 8493, BagIt v1.0, October 2018; Informational
sources.governing_meaning: Payload is opaque. Each bag needs at least one payload manifest; each manifest lists every payload file once. Tag manifests are optional, must list payload manifests, and must not list other tag manifests or payload files. bagit.txt is UTF-8 without BOM; remaining tag encoding should be UTF-8 but may differ for compatibility. A valid bag is complete with all manifest checksums verified. Tools must support SHA-256/SHA-512 and should default to SHA-512. The proposed SHA-256 choice is allowed. Fixity does not secure against active attacks.
sources.applicability: Confirms CR-4 and the analogous transfer mechanism. No completed bag, implementation conformance or audio semantics are established.

material_finding_source_map.classification: material incomplete source applicability / unreconciled consequential condition
material_finding_source_map.title: The final carries an obsolete broad XML-verification warning without reconciling released checks
material_finding_source_map.candidate_claim: MediaArea’s current XML-chunk help says aXML/iXML/XMP editing does not validate XML or schema instances and has no undo; the final treats this as a tool-specific caution.
material_finding_source_map.judgment: The quotation/paraphrase is accurate about the rolling help, but the operational source condition is materially incomplete. The proposal does not distinguish released syntactic parsing/warnings from absent format/schema conformance checks. The cited history already supplies the contradictory later change, and relevant public code resolves that distinction. The original brief requires relevant source code and released history where they bear on the proposal; obligation 3 requires investigated embedding conditions. All three stages leave this publicly answerable distinction unresolved.
material_finding_source_map.bounded_counterevidence: Schema/format validation and no-undo cautions remain supported; an XML warning is not blocking enforcement and does not certify valid metadata. Sidecar-first remains a reasonable local recommendation. No conclusion is made about corruption, deployment, consent or the behavior of an installed 26.08.1 binary.
material_finding_source_map.materiality: XML verification is a consequential safety/applicability condition for one investigated embedded metadata path. Discovery uses the broad warning to advise avoiding that path unless further controls are approved, the draft repeats it in obligation 3, the critic endorses it, and the final preserves it as a tool condition. Source attribution does not complete investigation of the visible release-history conflict. This is more than a citation-format issue even though the baseline recommendation can remain sensible.
material_finding_source_map.final_disposition: REMAINS; source-backed FAIL. No candidate repair or feedback performed.
